title: Region-Specific EEG Classification of Hypnotic Susceptibility Using a Sliding-Window 2D CNN: A Subject-Independent Evaluation
abstract: arXiv:2610.28427v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: We investigate whether a 2D Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) trained on minimally preprocessed EEG signals can classify hypnotic susceptibility across distinct brain regions. Sixty-two male participants (32 Control, 30 Guided Imagery / Hipno group) underwent a 20-minute EEG recording using a 256-channel EGI cap. A sliding-window approach evaluates all 10-second windows within the recording for each of seven predefined brain regions (prefrontal, frontal, temporal, central, parietal, occipital, and facial), yielding up to 868 independently trained models. Initial screening with a segment-level 90/10 random split showed that five regions exceeded the 0.67 accuracy threshold, with the occipital region achieving the highest mean accuracy (0.721) across 90.3% of windows. Subject-independent evaluation via Leave-One-Subject-Out (LOSO) cross-validation, however, substantially revised this picture: occipital performance collapsed to near-chance

translated_title: 基于滑动窗口二维卷积神经网络的催眠易感性脑区特异性脑电分类：一项被试独立评估研究
translated_abstract: 我们研究了在最小预处理的脑电信号上训练的二维卷积神经网络（CNN）能否跨不同脑区对催眠易感性进行分类。62名男性被试（32名对照组，30名引导意象/催眠组）使用256通道EGI脑电帽进行了20分钟的脑电记录。滑动窗口方法对七个预定义脑区（前额叶、额叶、颞叶、中央区、顶叶、枕叶和面部）记录中的所有10秒窗口进行评估，最多训练了868个独立模型。采用片段级90/10随机划分的初步筛查显示，五个脑区超过了0.67的准确率阈值，其中枕叶区在90.3%的窗口上取得了最高的平均准确率（0.721）。然而，通过留一被试交叉验证（LOSO）进行的被试独立评估大幅修正了这一结果：枕叶区的表现骤降至接近随机水平……
tldr: 该论文用滑动窗口2D CNN对脑电进行脑区特异性的催眠易感性分类，发现虽然随机划分筛查中枕叶区准确率最高（0.721），但在严格的留一被试交叉验证下表现骤降至接近随机水平，凸显了被试独立评估对脑电分类研究的关键意义。
en_tdlr: This paper applies a sliding-window 2D CNN for region-specific EEG classification of hypnotic susceptibility, showing that although the occipital region achieved the highest accuracy (0.721) under random-split screening, its performance collapsed to near-chance under subject-independent Leave-One-Subject-Out cross-validation, underscoring the critical importance of subject-independent evaluation in EEG classification research.
